tier_reason: README Benchmarks section gives the per-tier decode ratios vs lz4 --fast, lz4, lz4hc -9 and zstd -1 on Silesia, with public benchmark code (lzbench 2.3.1, driven by .github/workflows/benchmark.yml), flags (MOREFLAGS=-march=native), compilers (Clang 21, GCC 14) and CPU models; the lzbench maintainer's own README table (lzbench 2.4, gcc 15.2.0, AMD EPYC 9555P) independently lists zxc 0.14.1 ahead of LZ4 on decode at matched ratio.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 465 stars, 11 forks; zxc 0.14.1 is integrated in lzbench (listed 2026-09-20) and TurboBench (listed as added 2026/05)
corrections.caveats: README numbers are first party, but code, tool (lzbench), flags and CPUs are public and the CI benchmark workflow re-runs lzbench on ubuntu-latest and macos-26-xlarge. Independent check: the lzbench README (lzbench 2.4, gcc 15.2.0, single thread of AMD EPYC 9555P, turbo off) lists zxc 0.14.1 -1 at 8151 MB/s decode vs lz4 --fast -17 3977 MB/s (2.05x), -3 4716 vs lz4 3832 MB/s (1.23x), -6 3938 vs lz4hc -9 3703 MB/s (1.06x), with ratios 61.76/46.09/36.28% vs 62.15/47.60/36.75% (ratios derived from page data); zxc -7 is not in that table. The x86 gain at the high tier is small (1.06-1.19x); the win is largest on ARM64. Compression is much slower than LZ4 at -6 (9.04 vs 31.9 MB/s for lz4hc -9 in lzbench). Another repo (Vladexy88x/zxc) shows the same description and appears to be a copy. Repo is young.

notes: README table and ratio pairings match the record exactly. lzbench and TurboBench integration confirmed from their READMEs; lzbench's own run supports the decode lead at smaller margins than the README's x86 figures for -6.

tier_reason: Upgraded from B: the PVLDB 2020 paper (fsstcompression.pdf) states g++ 8.3.1 -O3 -march=native, LZ4 1.8.1 and an i9-7900X, and the repo's paper/ directory holds the replication package (Makefile with 'make experiments', compare.sh post-processing Table 1, linetest.cpp, filtertest.cpp, and the dbtext corpus), so code, compiler, flags and CPU are all public.

corrections.claimed_speedup: PVLDB 2020 paper Table 1 (22 dbtext sets, 8 MB files, single thread): FSST compression speed beats LZ4 on 21 of 22 sets (e.g. genome 1,307 vs 566 MB/s, uuid 1,113 vs 632, credentials 984 vs 439; LZ4 wins on hex 1,097 vs 944) with a higher compression factor on 21 of 22 (e.g. genome 3.32 vs 1.59, uuid 2.44 vs 1.55; LZ4 wins on urls 2.77 vs 2.16); paper text gives average factor 2.28x vs LZ4 1.70x. Decompression speed is mixed: FSST faster on 12 sets (e.g. genome 2,838 vs 1,126 MB/s, c_name 3,519 vs 2,960), LZ4 faster on 10 (e.g. hex 1,891 vs 1,546, email 2,388 vs 1,547) (counts derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed (PVLDB vol 13 no 12, 2020); numbers read from the paper PDF checked into the repo (via raw.githubusercontent.com). LZ4 version is old (1.8.1) with g++ 8.3.1. Decompression is on par with LZ4, slower on 10 of 22 sets; the main win is compression ratio, compression speed and per-string random access. File mode is LZ4's best case per the paper. Replication package (paper/ directory with dbtext corpus and Makefile) is in the repo; it needs Linux perf counters and LZ4 1.8.1 on PATH.

notes: All quoted Table 1 numbers match the paper. Tier raised to A because the replication package and dbtext corpus are in the repo's paper/ directory.

tier_reason: Independent TurboBench run by its author (powturbo) in zlib-ng issue 1486 on a Ryzen 6600HS compares igzip levels 0-3 against zlib levels 1-9 on silesia.tar; compiler and flags are not stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: zlib-ng issue 1486 (powturbo, TurboBench, silesia.tar, Ryzen 6600HS): igzip 1 compresses at 615.11 MB/s and ratio 36.9% vs zlib 1 at 127.47 MB/s and 36.5% (4.8x, derived from page data), and decompresses at 1020.09 vs 448.95 MB/s (2.3x, derived from page data). igzip 2: 598.69 MB/s at 36.1%; igzip decode ranges 969-1081 MB/s vs zlib 449-484 MB/s across levels. At higher levels zlib reaches better ratios (zlib 9: 31.9% at 15.55 MB/s) that igzip does not offer.
corrections.caveats: Ratios are only near-matched at level 1 (igzip 36.9% vs zlib 36.5%); igzip's best ratio (35.5%, level 3) is worse than zlib 6/9. The original record misread the zlib_ng 9 row (27.79 MB/s, 32.2%) as zlib 9; zlib 9 is 15.55 MB/s at 31.9%. libdeflate decodes slightly faster than igzip in the same table (1075-1134 MB/s). Compiler and flags unstated in the issue. Repo README lists features but gives no numbers.

notes: Record's number for 'zlib level 9' was actually the zlib_ng 9 row; claimed_speedup rewritten with the level-1 near-matched pair and decode numbers that the record said were not seen. License BSD-3-Clause confirmed from LICENSE file; last commit 2026-09-30 confirmed.
